title: Cloud Test Machine power
summary: A Test Machine whose settings record cloud_instance_id is an EC2 instance powered from the executing machine with the project's aws-admin key. Contract materialization (resolve_contract_host_control), yoke test-machine operations and declared-host Commands start a stopped instance, wait for instance-running and a login probe (on Windows, the WSL Python the first host command uses), then continue. The last lease release stops it: any call whose release leaves the host free (no waiter's turn reserved) names it in the response field released_test_machines, and the calling client's transport, whatever command or process it is, stops it while holding the host's own lease through claims.coordination_claim.acquire_if_free, which refuses instead of joining the waiting line. A concurrent acquirer queues behind that hold and its start waits out stopping. A Command that runs several yoke test-machine operations must declare method_config.test_machine (authoring also catches yoke --env prod test-machine), so the plan holds the host across them. Start failures refuse with test_machine_power_start_failed, test_machine_power_ssh_unreachable or test_machine_power_aws_unavailable; stop problems print test_machine_power_stop_failed or test_machine_power_hold_failed and never change the call's result. An instance without an Elastic IP is never stopped (test_machine_power_stop_skipped). Machines without cloud_instance_id are untouched.
